items.summary: After the 11-petitioner writ was filed, Rahul Gandhi posted on X thanking marchers and supporters, saying the day showed 'the people of India are not going to be intimidated' and 'We will not accept being bullied.' He asked where the 'cowards of the RSS' - who he alleged beat young protesters over the weekend - were, calling them and PM Modi 'bullies' who 'can only use power to fight.' CATCH-UP: posted ~10:26 PM IST Oct 12 (reporterworldnews live key update), never logged by earlier runs.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi's post-march X statement: thanks supporters, calls PM Modi and RSS 'bullies'

items.summary: AAP leader and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh wrote to PM Narendra Modi demanding a special Parliament session 'at the earliest' to discuss alleged 'vote-chori', the deletion of 13+ crore names from voter lists, and the police crackdown on protesters demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. New parliamentary front in the agitation. CATCH-UP: letter reported ~7:49 PM IST Oct 12 (reporterworldnews live), never logged by earlier runs.
items.title: AAP MP Sanjay Singh writes to PM Modi demanding special Parliament session on 'vote-chori'

items.summary: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey told ANI that Rahul Gandhi 'wants to destroy the country's constitution,' questioning the march to the Supreme Court ('Have you ever heard from 1947 until today that people go to the Supreme Court to protest?'), drawing parallels with the Emergency imposed by Indira Gandhi, and saying constitutional authorities can only be challenged via elections, no-confidence motions or impeachment. CATCH-UP: ~7:39 PM IST Oct 12 (reporterworldnews live), never logged by earlier runs.
items.title: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey: Rahul Gandhi 'wants to destroy the Constitution', invokes Emergency

items.summary: Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju posted on X that protest is every citizen's right but 'brazenly abusing constitutional authorities is deplorable,' called Congress 'directionless,' and in a second post alleged the judiciary would be Congress's next target, claiming 'all anti-India gangs are joining hands.' CATCH-UP: ~6:36 PM IST Oct 12 (reporterworldnews live), never logged by earlier runs.
items.title: Union minister Kiren Rijiju calls Congress 'directionless', says abusing constitutional authorities 'deplorable'

items.summary: The Kerala Congress's official X handle posted 'Dear Surya Kant, if law and order is not your domain, resign now. We will find your replacement who can handle it' - then deleted it after backlash. Rijiju shared a screenshot alleging the judiciary is Congress's next target; BJP Kerala unit accused Congress of Emergency-era judiciary intimidation; the SC Bar Association condemned remarks seeking the CJI's resignation as undermining the judiciary; Congress MP Pawan Khera distanced the party, calling the post 'completely incorrect.' CATCH-UP: row broke ~7:26 PM IST Oct 12 (article updated 11:56 PM IST), never logged by earlier runs.
items.title: Kerala Congress deletes X post demanding CJI's resignation over 'not my domain' remark; SCBA condemns

items.summary: CPI Rajya Sabha MP P Sandosh Kumar wrote to HM Amit Shah alleging 'widespread harassment, detention and confinement' of journalists covering the anti-CEC protests in Delhi, claiming one female news-portal correspondent was 'brutally dragged and detained,' and arguing PIB accreditation cannot be a prerequisite for reporting from public spaces; he accused authorities of trying to 'conceal police excesses.' CATCH-UP: ~7:08 PM IST Oct 12 (reporterworldnews live), never logged by earlier runs.
items.title: CPI MP P Sandosh Kumar writes to Amit Shah over alleged harassment of journalists covering protests

items.summary: On the sidelines of the NHRC's 33rd anniversary event at Vigyan Bhawan, CJI Surya Kant told reporters the Delhi protests and restrictions are 'Ye law and order ka mudda hai. Ye mera vishay nahin hai' (a law-and-order issue, not my domain), declined to comment on the opposition's march to the Supreme Court, and reiterated that the court's doors are open to all. CATCH-UP: Monday Oct 12 (reporterworldnews live 04:10 PM IST), never logged by earlier runs.
items.title: CJI Surya Kant: Delhi protests a 'law and order' matter, 'not my domain'; declines comment on march

items.summary: CJP's backup X handle @Cockroachisback posted that 'Modi Govt's brutal manhandling of peaceful protesters is making headlines across the world,' calling it a 'dictator's desperate attempt to save his traitor friend' that is 'costing India dearly' - the party's global-attention framing of the crackdown. CATCH-UP: ~7:42 PM IST Oct 12 (reporterworldnews live), never logged by earlier runs.
items.title: CJP backup handle: 'brutal manhandling of peaceful protesters is making headlines across the world'

items.summary: Former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee, who joined the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court, told reporters the movement seeks 'justice for the sake of humanity.' CATCH-UP: ~7:32 PM IST Oct 12 (reporterworldnews live), never logged by earlier runs.
items.title: Mamata Banerjee on joining the march: 'We are demanding justice for the sake of humanity'
